system.summary: One syllabary for the letters of Charles V and Prince Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga: consonant bases take a vowel mark (one dot a, bar e, two dots i, raised o, raised s), bare signs give letters, with homophones and a small code of word-like tokens.

diacritics.note: One dot, bar, two dots, raised o and raised s select the vowel of a consonant base. Dots written under a sign cancel it.

system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the rows of key.tsv; sign names are the transcriber's. Code words seen: dide Su Magestad, quod Embaxador, gaces Rey de Francia, em franceses, gien vuestra, mus para, and on 14 Nov Pollo, vela, inta, nep (context only).

prior_solution.where: Opened 3 Nov 2026: Calendar of State Papers Spain IX (Nov 1549, pp. 465-481), Calendar of State Papers Venice V (Nov 1549), Treccani DBI "Gonzaga, Ferrante": none prints the 14 Nov letter. Not opened: Corpus documental de Carlos V vol. III, Pastor XII, Robertson, Rodríguez-Salgado, Brandi, Motta, Gosellini, Solmi, Druffel, the Simancas minutes (Estado 1196). Whether the letter or its minute is printed is unknown.

conditions.human_role: WAINUT chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (key frozen before tests, blind passes, independent check). AI agents transcribed, built the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention.
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT), vision-capable for the transcription

solution.what: Fetched the Estense letters by IIIF, one request a second. Marginal decipherments found on c. 28r and c. 64v that the catalogue does not list.
c. 12r transcribed twice, signs first; 20 of 235 signs differ; the passes are dependent.
Table derived by aligning c. 12r with the contemporary decipherment on c. 14r, extended with cc. 9r-9v against c. 11, then frozen.
Frozen table on 1547 9v lines 11-16 (0.888 / 0.857) and 13 May 1549 (0.978 / 0.932) against contemporary clear, not blind; 200 shuffled tables max 0.431 / 0.374.

Blind shape pass with the frozen table: 30 Sep 1549, 408 signs, 0.728 / 0.595 (shuffled max 0.420 / 0.532); 20 Nov 1549, 140 signs, 0.652 / 0.323 (shuffled max 0.519 / 0.355). 20 Nov fails on runs of 4+.
14 Nov 1549 decoded and iterated against the images; the key extended on it. D24-F04 first gave nonsense and were re-read at zoom.

Independent agent read D14-E03 from crops before opening the transcription, with the table in view: 39 of 425 signs differ (9.2%). c. 10r at half scale: 43 of 212 (20.3%). It found 76 unmarked departures in the reading and a wrong headline.
Ten lines corrected at zoom, eight tokens settled, every departure marked and checked by alignment, Philip decryptions regenerated. 14 Nov: 811 of 910 words verbatim, 864 with repairs.
CSP Spain IX, CSP Venice V and the Treccani DBI opened; none prints the letter. Corpus documental III and the monographs not opened.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The table was built by aligning c. 12r with the contemporary decipherment on c. 14r and cc. 9r-9v with c. 11, frozen, tested on held-out letters, then extended on the 14 Nov letter.
outcome.fraction_read_source: scripts/check_marks.py on the four documents read in part: 1,017 of 1,147 words verbatim from the signs (14 Nov 811 of 910; c. 10r 75 of 80; c. 28r D, E 56 of 66; c. 26r 75 of 91). With marked repairs 1,086 of 1,147. The three letters decoded, not read, and the letters not started are outside this figure.

texts.label: Charles V to Ferrante Gonzaga, Brussels, 14 Nov 1549
texts.summary: Charles forbids Ferrante's plan to conclude terms with Ottavio Farnese over Parma, gives his reasons, and approves only a private settlement. Ferrante may act in two cases: if Camillo Orsini plays a trick and Parma leaves the Church's hands, or if Orazio or another enters Parma by a deal with France or otherwise, when he is to try to make himself master of the city with dexterity and dissimulation. Otherwise nothing is to be started.

texts.label: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, Valladolid, 4 Aug 1548, c. 10r
texts.summary: Philip approves what Ferrante writes on Genoa, refers him to a letter to Ambassador Figueroa, and asks for prompt news of the King of France's descent into Italy.

texts.label: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, Madrid, 24 Nov 1551, c. 28r
texts.summary: Thanks for the guard of Nice; the business of Siena seems to go well. Passage C, on Parma and the Mirandola, is covered by a marginal decipherment.

texts.label: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga, Madrid, 24 Nov 1551, c. 26r
texts.summary: The Germans sent by the Emperor should help finish matters; thanks for a paper on Siena. The vicariate passage rests on broken words.

texts.label: Philip to Ferrante Gonzaga: 25 Jun 1546, 14 Mar 1553, and the letter catalogued 16 Jun 1563
texts.summary: One rough blind pass decoded with the table. Runs of words appear; no sense is claimed.

texts.label: Philip, 8 Mar 1549, c. 12r: covered by c. 14r
texts.summary: Transcription job, not a break: the key was built on it. The Emperor orders Philip to write to Figueroa on Genoa.

texts.label: Philip, 23 May 1547, cc. 9r-9v: covered by c. 11
texts.summary: Transcription job, not a break. After the death of Francis I: the Piedmont frontier and Siena.

texts.label: Charles V, 13 May 1549, c. 30r: covered by c. 29r
texts.summary: Transcription job, not a break. Ferrante is to work out secretly where money and materials for "la obra" can come from.

texts.label: Charles V, 30 Sep and 20 Nov 1549: covered by marginal decipherments
texts.summary: Transcription jobs, not breaks, and not yet editions. 30 Sep: a French plot on Nice. 20 Nov: after the news of Paul III's death, no move on Parma and no war on the Church.
